dimensions.assessment: Affects low-income households seeking home energy assistance and state agencies administering grants.
dimensions.evidence: a State may use any grant made under section 2602 of such Act (42 U.S.C. 8621) to make payments under section 2605(b)(2) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)) to households with incomes which do not exceed 75 percent of the State median income

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative flexibility for states and potentially broader eligibility for households needing energy assistance.
No specific new appropriations are authorized, but existing grant funds may be distributed differently among households.
Modifies household income eligibility criteria for a single fiscal year under an existing statute.
dimensions.evidence: for fiscal year 2027 a State may use any grant made under section 2602 of such Act

dimensions.assessment: The specific income eligibility change is explicitly limited to fiscal year 2027.
dimensions.evidence: for fiscal year 2027 a State may use any grant

missing_information: Exact number of additional households that will become eligible across participating states.
Total dollar amounts of grants that will be reallocated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill allows states to raise the household income eligibility threshold for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program to 75 percent of the State median income for fiscal year 2027.
